Langflow Python runtime spawning shell / nsenter / base64-decoded child process AIExploitation High
Detects the on-host manifestation of Langflow RCE: the Python/uvicorn interpreter spawning a shell, nsenter, docker, or a base64-decoded exec() payload. JADEPUFFER built six iterative scripts, each base64-encoded and decoded inside exec() to evade shell-level signatures, before breaking out to the host. Rationale: Pairs a narrow parent set (Langflow's python/uvicorn runtime) with breakout child binaries and the exact evasion primitives from the article (base64-decoded exec(), nsenter, docker.sock) — a parent+child combination, not a bare interpreter match. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-evolves-the-agentic-threat-actor-deploys-ransomware-built-to-destroy-ai-models • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/jadepuffer-agentic-attacks-now-target-ai-model-data-with-ransomware/
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1059.004 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow custom-component code that legitimately shells out (e.g. subprocess calls in a user-authored flow)
  • DevOps CI jobs running python that invoke docker build/run on the same host
  • Data-science notebooks under uvicorn spawning bash for package installs
  • Health-check or entrypoint scripts wrapping the Langflow process
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker build","docker-compose") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "ci-runner")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full InitiatingProcessCommandLine and child command line; decode any base64 (`base64 -d`) and inspect for docker/nsenter breakout logic or ENCFORGE references. 2) Contain: kill the offending python/child tree, snapshot the container, and cut the host off the network. 3) Hunt: check the same host for privileged container creation, nsenter, and mass .locked file writes; review Langflow access logs for the preceding /api/v1/validate/code POSTs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","langflow","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","nsenter","docker")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("nsenter","/var/run/docker.sock","docker.sock","b64decode","exec(")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","langflow","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","nsenter","docker")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("nsenter","docker.sock","b64decode","exec(")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Docker-socket privileged container breakout + nsenter host escape AIExploitation High
Detects JADEPUFFER's host breakout: abusing the exposed /var/run/docker.sock to create a Privileged:true container with PidMode=host and the root filesystem bind-mounted, then pivoting onto the host with nsenter. This is the step that turned container RCE into host-root and enabled the ENCFORGE run. Rationale: Directly encodes the article's breakout recipe — Privileged:true + PidMode:host + root bind-mount via /var/run/docker.sock, then nsenter onto the host. These flag combinations are near-unique to container escape and rare in benign ops. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-evolves-the-agentic-threat-actor-deploys-ransomware-built-to-destroy-ai-models • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/jadepuffer-ai-model-ransomware/
ATT&CKT1611 T1610 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate privileged sidecars/agents (monitoring, CNI, storage drivers) launched with --privileged --pid=host
  • Admin troubleshooting via nsenter into a container namespace
  • Node-management DaemonSets that mount the host filesystem
  • Backup tooling bind-mounting / read-write for volume snapshots
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubelet","containerd","dockerd") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cni","csi-","node-exporter"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the parent of the docker/nsenter process — if it's the Langflow python runtime or a web-tier user, treat as breakout; review the container's create parameters for Privileged/PidMode/host mounts. 2) Contain: stop and remove the rogue container, revoke docker-socket access from the app container, isolate the node. 3) Hunt: scan the host filesystem for ENCFORGE (hidden /.lockd, self-deleting Go binary) and mass .locked writes; audit every container with docker.sock mounted.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "nsenter" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--target 1","-t 1","--mount","--pid","--net"))
   or (FileName =~ "docker" and ProcessCommandLine has "--privileged" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--pid=host","--pid host","--net=host","-v /:","/:/host"))
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "/var/run/docker.sock" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Privileged","PidMode","/proc/"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (TargetProcessName endswith "nsenter" and TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("--target 1","-t 1","--mount","--pid"))
   or (TargetProcessName endswith "docker" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--privileged" and TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("--pid=host","--net=host","-v /:"))
   or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "/var/run/docker.sock" and TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("Privileged","PidMode"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ENCFORGE Go ransomware execution — hashes, hidden path, and cmdline flags AIActions on Objectives Medium
Alerts on execution of the ENCFORGE binary by its packed/unpacked SHA-256 hashes, its hidden staging path (/.lockd), stable project strings (encfile, keyforge), and its distinctive operator flags (--try-run, --lock, --include, --task-id gcp_h1/gcp_test). These strings survive recompilation and are the report's named detection anchors. Rationale: Uses the article's exact hashes (packed 8cb0c223…, unpacked ea7822ea…, plus the third IOC), the hidden /.lockd staging path, recompilation-stable strings encfile/keyforge, and operator flags --try-run/--lock/--include/--task-id gcp_h1 — all named as durable detection anchors. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-evolves-the-agentic-threat-actor-deploys-ransomware-built-to-destroy-ai-models • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/jadepuffer-agentic-attacks-now-target-ai-model-data-with-ransomware/
ATT&CKT1486 T1027.002 T1070.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • An internal tool coincidentally named encfile (rare on Linux servers)
  • Legitimate archival/CLI tools using a --include glob flag without the other anchors
  • Threat-intel researchers detonating the sample in a sandbox
  • A backup job whose binary happens to live under a dot-prefixed path
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the SHA-256 against the three IOCs and capture the full command line (task-id, --include globs) before the binary self-deletes; snapshot volatile memory if still running. 2) Contain: kill the process, isolate the host, and preserve /proc image and any ransom notes; the binary deletes itself, so grab it fast. 3) Hunt: enumerate .locked files and README/HOW_TO_DECRYPT/README_DECRYPT notes across model stores; search other hosts for the same hashes and the e78393397@proton.me contact string.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in ("8cb0c223b018cecef1d990ec81c67b826eb3c30d54f06193cf69969e9a8baea2","ea7822eac6cecef7746c606b862b4d3034856caf754c4cf69533662637905328","ab9824b61587c77a8d8649545cdbdc63ed2c384e45c9aba534e3f457f96efa7a")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--try-run","--task-id gcp_h1","--task-id gcp_test","keyforge","encfile")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "--lock" and ProcessCommandLine has "--include")
   or FolderPath has "/.lockd"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in ("8cb0c223b018cecef1d990ec81c67b826eb3c30d54f06193cf69969e9a8baea2","ea7822eac6cecef7746c606b862b4d3034856caf754c4cf69533662637905328","ab9824b61587c77a8d8649545cdbdc63ed2c384e45c9aba534e3f457f96efa7a")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("--try-run","--task-id gcp_h1","--task-id gcp_test","keyforge","encfile")
   or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "--lock" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--include")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mass .locked rename + ENCFORGE ransom-note drop on AI model stores AIActions on Objectives High
Detects ENCFORGE's impact stage: bulk renaming of files to .locked (encrypting AI model weights, SafeTensors, GGUF/GGML, ONNX, FAISS, Parquet/Arrow, NumPy) and creation of its README, HOW_TO_DECRYPT, and README_DECRYPT ransom notes. Thresholds on rename volume per process to catch the encryption sweep. Rationale: Anchors on ENCFORGE's exact impact artifacts from the article: the .locked rename extension, the three named ransom notes (README, HOW_TO_DECRYPT, README_DECRYPT), and a >=25-file-per-5-min threshold to distinguish an encryption sweep from single-file activity. Model-file extensions (.safetensors/.gguf/.faiss/.parquet) surface as the pre-rename names. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-evolves-the-agentic-threat-actor-deploys-ransomware-built-to-destroy-ai-models • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/jadepuffer-ai-model-ransomware/
ATT&CKT1486 T1489
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate app that uses a .locked lockfile convention (single files, low volume — filtered by the >=25 threshold)
  • A git repo or package creating a plain README (note-only clause; restrict to HOW_TO_DECRYPT/README_DECRYPT to suppress)
  • Bulk file-format migration jobs on a model store producing many renames
  • Backup/restore tooling rewriting many model files in a short window
Suppression filter
| where not (Actor in~ ("restic","borg","veeamagent","rsync") and LockedCount < 25)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess driving the .locked renames and correlate to the ENCFORGE binary/hashes; open a ransom note (HOW_TO_DECRYPT) and confirm the e78393397@proton.me contact. 2) Contain: kill the process, isolate the host, and immediately protect/immutable-lock any remaining model, vector-index, and training-data volumes. 3) Hunt: quantify encrypted files by extension, verify offline/immutable snapshots exist for the affected model stores, and sweep other AI hosts for the same process and .locked artifacts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (ActionType == "FileRenamed" and FileName endswith ".locked")
   or (ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified") and FileName in~ ("HOW_TO_DECRYPT","README_DECRYPT","README"))
| extend ModelTarget = tostring(PreviousFileName)
| summarize LockedCount = countif(FileName endswith ".locked"),
            NoteCount = countif(FileName in~ ("HOW_TO_DECRYPT","README_DECRYPT","README")),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleFolders = make_set(FolderPath, 10),
            SampleModelFiles = make_set(ModelTarget, 10),
            Actor = any(InitiatingProcessFileName), ActorCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where LockedCount >= 25 or NoteCount >= 1
| order by LockedCount desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (EventType == "FileRenamed" and TargetFileName endswith ".locked")
   or (EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified") and TargetFileName in~ ("HOW_TO_DECRYPT","README_DECRYPT","README"))
| summarize LockedCount = countif(TargetFileName endswith ".locked"),
            NoteCount = countif(TargetFileName in~ ("HOW_TO_DECRYPT","README_DECRYPT","README")),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), SampleFiles = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10),
            Actor = any(ActingProcessName)
            by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where LockedCount >= 25 or NoteCount >= 1
| order by LockedCount desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-3248")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-3248")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")

     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents

| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host

| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("8cb0c223b018cecef1d990ec81c67b826eb3c30d54f06193cf69969e9a8baea2", "ea7822eac6cecef7746c606b862b4d3034856caf754c4cf69533662637905328", "ab9824b61587c77a8d8649545cdbdc63ed2c384e45c9aba534e3f457f96efa7a") or SHA1 in~ ("8cb0c223b018cecef1d990ec81c67b826eb3c30d54f06193cf69969e9a8baea2", "ea7822eac6cecef7746c606b862b4d3034856caf754c4cf69533662637905328", "ab9824b61587c77a8d8649545cdbdc63ed2c384e45c9aba534e3f457f96efa7a") or MD5 in~ ("8cb0c223b018cecef1d990ec81c67b826eb3c30d54f06193cf69969e9a8baea2", "ea7822eac6cecef7746c606b862b4d3034856caf754c4cf69533662637905328", "ab9824b61587c77a8d8649545cdbdc63ed2c384e45c9aba534e3f457f96efa7a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("8cb0c223b018cecef1d990ec81c67b826eb3c30d54f06193cf69969e9a8baea2", "ea7822eac6cecef7746c606b862b4d3034856caf754c4cf69533662637905328", "ab9824b61587c77a8d8649545cdbdc63ed2c384e45c9aba534e3f457f96efa7a") or SHA1 in~ ("8cb0c223b018cecef1d990ec81c67b826eb3c30d54f06193cf69969e9a8baea2", "ea7822eac6cecef7746c606b862b4d3034856caf754c4cf69533662637905328", "ab9824b61587c77a8d8649545cdbdc63ed2c384e45c9aba534e3f457f96efa7a") or MD5 in~ ("8cb0c223b018cecef1d990ec81c67b826eb3c30d54f06193cf69969e9a8baea2", "ea7822eac6cecef7746c606b862b4d3034856caf754c4cf69533662637905328", "ab9824b61587c77a8d8649545cdbdc63ed2c384e45c9aba534e3f457f96efa7a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["8cb0c223b018cecef1d990ec81c67b826eb3c30d54f06193cf69969e9a8baea2", "ea7822eac6cecef7746c606b862b4d3034856caf754c4cf69533662637905328", "ab9824b61587c77a8d8649545cdbdc63ed2c384e45c9aba534e3f457f96efa7a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Critical

Critical ServiceNow AI Platform Flaw Exploited for Unauthenticated Code Execution

The Hacker News
2026-07-21 14 use cases 7 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Threat actors are now exploiting a recently disclosed critical security flaw impacting ServiceNow AI Platform, according to Defused Cyber. In a post shared on X, the threat intelligence firm said it's observing in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-6875 (CVSS score: 9.5), a sandbox escape vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to run arbitrary code. Patches for the flaw were

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] ServiceNow CVE-2026-6875 pre-auth RCE: POST/GET to /assessment_thanks.do · [LLM] ServiceNow CVE-2026-6875 sandbox-escape gadget markers in assessment_thanks.do request · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] ServiceNow node / MID Server Java process spawning OS shell (CVE-2026-6875 post-exploit) · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
ServiceNow CVE-2026-6875 pre-auth RCE: POST/GET to /assessment_thanks.do AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to the ServiceNow pre-auth sink /assessment_thanks.do, the endpoint Defused observed being exploited in the wild for CVE-2026-6875 (Searchlight documented sysparm_assessable_type as the unsanitized GlideRecord parameter). This endpoint is rarely touched by legitimate anonymous traffic, so requests carrying the sysparm_assessable_type parameter from external sources are a high-fidelity exploitation signal. Rationale: Anchored on the article's named pre-auth endpoint /assessment_thanks.do plus the Searchlight-documented sysparm_assessable_type parameter; both are article/CVE-specific rather than generic web patterns, and the endpoint sees almost no legitimate anonymous traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://slcyber.io/research-center/smashing-the-servicenow-sandbox-pre-authentication-rce/ • https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB3137947 • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-servicenow-code-execution-flaw-now-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/20/servicenow-cve-2026-6875-exploited/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate end users completing a ServiceNow survey/assessment (the /assessment_thanks.do landing page) — but those requests carry a valid session cookie and no sysparm_assessable_type injection value
  • Authorized vulnerability scanners (Tenable/Qualys/Nuclei) probing the CVE-2026-6875 template
  • Internal ServiceNow health-check or synthetic monitors hitting the endpoint
  • Penetration testers validating patch status against the sink
Suppression filter
| where WebUser == "" or WebUser == "-" or isempty(WebUser) or Query has "sysparm_assessable_type"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request line and the sysparm_assessable_type value from the surfaced Query field; confirm the source IP is external/unauthenticated and check the ServiceNow instance version against the patched builds (Zurich P7b/P9, Yokohama P12HF1b/P13, Australia P2, Brazil EA/GA). 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, force the instance behind auth/allowlist, and if unpatched schedule emergency upgrade; capture the MID Server hosts the instance connects to. 3) Hunt: correlate the source IP to any subsequent /assessment_thanks.do hits, look for new admin accounts on the instance, and pivot to UC3 to check whether the app node or MID Server spawned shells shortly after.
union isfuzzy=true

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where csUriStem has "/assessment_thanks.do" or csUriQuery has "sysparm_assessable_type"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIP=cIP, TargetHost=Computer, Method=csMethod, Uri=csUriStem, Query=csUriQuery, WebUser=csUserName, HttpStatus=scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent),
(CommonSecurityLog

| sort by TimeGenerated desc

ServiceNow CVE-2026-6875 sandbox-escape gadget markers in assessment_thanks.do request AIExploitation Medium
Execution-phase hunt for CVE-2026-6875 exploitation payloads: requests to /assessment_thanks.do whose sysparm_assessable_type value carries ServiceNow sandbox-escape / GlideRecord-injection gadget markers (Rhino Packages.java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime, eval(, javascript:, GlideRecord). Because Defused reported a second gadget chain that varies from the public PoC, this targets the payload shape rather than a single byte-signature. Rationale: Combines the article's exact endpoint/parameter with Rhino/GlideScript sandbox-escape gadget tokens (Packages.java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime) that are the canonical ServiceNow RCE primitive corroborated by Searchlight's write-up; matched on payload shape to survive the second gadget chain Defused reported. Cross-checked against: • https://slcyber.io/research-center/smashing-the-servicenow-sandbox-pre-authentication-rce/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/poc-for-servicenow-sandbox-rce-vulnerability/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/20/servicenow-cve-2026-6875-exploited/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Web/WAF logs that do not capture POST bodies will simply not match — verify body/context logging is enabled before trusting silence
  • Security scanners (Nuclei/Burp) firing CVE-2026-6875 or generic RCE templates against the endpoint
  • Legitimate survey submissions that coincidentally contain 'eval' or '$(' substrings in free-text answers reflected into the query string
  • Internal red-team payload testing after patching
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the decoded sysparm_assessable_type value and confirm it contains an executable gadget (Packages.java.*, getRuntime, javascript:) vs benign text; note source IP and whether the request returned a 200. 2) Contain: block the source IP, and on the ServiceNow node/MID Server hunt for spawned OS processes (UC3) and outbound connections initiated by the java process in the minutes after the request. 3) Hunt: sweep all web/WAF logs for the same gadget markers across other ServiceNow endpoints and other source IPs, and validate the instance is on a patched build.

ServiceNow node / MID Server Java process spawning OS shell (CVE-2026-6875 post-exploit) AIInstallation Medium
Post-exploitation of CVE-2026-6875 lets attackers run OS commands on the ServiceNow instance and on connected MID Server proxies. This flags the ServiceNow Java app node or MID Server wrapper (java.exe / wrapper*.exe) spawning cmd/powershell/sh/bash and LOLBins on self-hosted deployments — a strong indicator the sandbox escape reached OS command execution. Rationale: Article states exploitation yields code execution on the instance and 'commands on connected proxy servers' (MID Servers); ServiceNow app nodes and MID Servers run on the Tanuki Java Service Wrapper (java.exe/wrapper.exe), so that parent spawning a shell on self-hosted hosts is a tight post-exploit pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://slcyber.io/research-center/smashing-the-servicenow-sandbox-pre-authentication-rce/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-servicenow-code-execution-flaw-now-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/20/servicenow-cve-2026-6875-exploited/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.001 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • ServiceNow MID Server Discovery/Orchestration legitimately launching PowerShell/SSH probe commands against targets
  • Other Java applications on the same host (Jenkins, Elasticsearch, Tomcat apps) spawning cmd/sh for plugins or build steps
  • Admin-initiated troubleshooting scripts run from the ServiceNow service context
  • Monitoring/backup agents wrapped in Java invoking shell helpers
Suppression filter
| where ChildCmd !has 'mid.probe' and ChildCmd !has_any ('Get-WmiObject Win32_OperatingSystem','powershell -f probe','Discovery') and ParentCmd !has 'jenkins' and ParentPath !has 'elasticsearch'
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the child ChildCmd/CommandLine — Discovery probes reference mid.* patterns and target hosts, whereas attacker shells show recon (whoami, ipconfig, curl to unknown IPs) or download activity; confirm the host is a patched ServiceNow node/MID Server. 2) Contain: isolate the host from the network, revoke the MID Server credentials, and rotate the instance's connected-account secrets; block any outbound IP the shell contacted. 3) Hunt: correlate the spawn time back to a UC1/UC2 /assessment_thanks.do hit on the fronting web tier, check for new local/admin accounts, scheduled tasks/services for persistence, and repeat the process sweep across all MID Server hosts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ('java.exe','wrapper.exe','wrapper-windows-x86-64.exe','java')
| where FileName in~ ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','pwsh.exe','bash','sh','bash.exe','wscript.exe','cscript.exe','curl.exe','certutil.exe','bitsadmin.exe')
| where AccountName !endswith '$'
| where AccountName !in~ ('system','local service','network service')
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentProc=InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildProc=FileName, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith '\\java.exe' or ParentProcessName endswith '\\wrapper.exe' or ParentProcessName endswith '\\wrapper-windows-x86-64.exe'
| where NewProcessName endswith '\\cmd.exe' or NewProcessName endswith '\\powershell.exe' or NewProcessName endswith '\\pwsh.exe' or NewProcessName endswith '\\wscript.exe' or NewProcessName endswith '\\cscript.exe' or NewProcessName endswith '\\curl.exe' or NewProcessName endswith '\\certutil.exe' or NewProcessName endswith '\\bitsadmin.exe'
| where SubjectUserName !endswith '$'
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-6875")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-6875")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-6875")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-6875")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,

Vulnerable node-tar (<=7.5.18) present on hosts — CVE-2026-59873 decompression-bomb DoS exposure AIWeaponization High
Surfaces every host where Defender/vuln-scanner telemetry reports the npm 'tar' package at or below 7.5.18, the range vulnerable to CVE-2026-59873 (unbounded decompressed-data DoS / Gzip bomb). This is the attack-surface inventory pivot: any service extracting untrusted archives with this version can be forced to exhaust disk/CPU with a tiny crafted input. Fixed in 7.5.19. Rationale: Pivots on the exact CVE id and the concrete affected range from the advisory (npm 'tar' <= 7.5.18, fixed 7.5.19). CVE-id equality in TVM/scanner data is a high-fidelity exposure list with near-zero FP — the only 'noise' is remediated-but-not-rescanned hosts. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-59874 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw • https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-59874 • https://github.com/isaacs/node-tar/security
ATT&CKT1499.004
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Host patched to 7.5.19+ but not yet re-scanned, so TVM snapshot is stale
  • 'tar' package pinned inside a container image layer that never extracts untrusted input (internal build tarballs only)
  • Nested/transitive copy of tar in node_modules of a dev-only dependency not reachable at runtime
  • Scanner fingerprints a vendored copy of tar sources without a functioning install
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the flagged host actually runs a service that extracts attacker-supplied archives (npm registry mirror, CI/CD artifact unpack, file-upload/import feature) — internal-only tarball handling is lower priority. 2) Contain: schedule `npm i tar@7.5.19` (or bump the transitive pin via overrides/resolutions) on internet-facing extractors first; add a temporary reverse-proxy body-size cap on upload endpoints. 3) Hunt: pull last 7d of file-write telemetry for the host's node processes and run UC2 to check whether a decompression bomb was already attempted.

node.js process rapidly writing multi-GB file during archive extraction (CVE-2026-59873 gzip-bomb impact) AIActions on Objectives Low
Hunts the runtime signature of the node-tar decompression bomb: a node process extracting an archive and writing an abnormally large single file (multi-GB) from a tiny compressed input, driving toward disk exhaustion. Article-specific because the vuln has no total-bytes/entry-count guard, so extraction writes far more data than the input warrants. Rationale: Targets the article's core impact — node-tar writes gigabytes to disk from a negligible compressed stream because there is no cumulative-bytes limit. Pivots on node as the initiating process plus an anomalous single-file size / write-volume, the observable footprint of the Gzip bomb described in the PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw • https://github.com/isaacs/node-tar/security
ATT&CKT1499.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate large-artifact extraction in CI (multi-GB container layers, ML model tarballs, dataset archives)
  • Node-based backup/restore or migration jobs that genuinely unpack large archives
  • Log-rotation or cache builds where a node service writes a large single file
  • Package-mirror sync (e.g. Verdaccio/nexus) unpacking large legitimate packages
  • Electron/build tooling emitting a large bundled asset
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("backup","restore","webpack","electron-builder","model","dataset") or FolderPath has_any ("\\ci\\","\\build\\","\\artifacts\\","/ci/","/build/","/artifacts/"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: check the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and FolderPath — is this a known CI/build/backup job writing to an expected artifact path, or an internet-facing upload/import service writing to a temp/extraction dir? Correlate the host against UC1 (is tar<=7.5.18 present?). 2) Contain: if unexplained, kill the node PID and quarantine the source archive; add disk-quota/ulimit on the extraction directory and a body-size limit on the upload endpoint. 3) Hunt: search the same host+window for the inbound tiny archive (small POST/upload immediately preceding the write burst) and for repeated attempts across other extractor hosts.

| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| summarize MaxFileSize = max(FileSize), Writes = count(), FirstWrite = min(Timestamp), LastWrite = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where MaxFileSize > 2147483648   // >2GB single file from a node extraction; gzip-bomb hallmark vs tiny input
| extend WriteWindowSec = datetime_diff('second', LastWrite, FirstWrite)
| order by MaxFileSize desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActingProcessName has "node"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| summarize MaxFileSize = max(TargetFileSize), Writes = count(), FirstWrite = min(TimeGenerated), LastWrite = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where MaxFileSize > 2147483648   // >2GB single file written by node during extraction
| extend WriteWindowSec = datetime_diff('second', LastWrite, FirstWrite)
| order by MaxFileSize desc

LightRAG destructive document ops post-bypass (DELETE /documents, clear_cache, unauth upload) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the impact stage of CVE-2026-61740 exploitation: destructive or ingestion calls to the LightRAG document API — DELETE /documents (wipes the corpus), /documents/clear_cache (destroys LLM/embedding caches) and /documents/upload|scan|file_batch (attacker-controlled ingestion). These are inherently rare, high-consequence operations that map directly to the advisory's confidentiality/integrity/availability impact. Rationale: Uses the exact destructive LightRAG endpoints named in the advisory impact section — DELETE /documents, /documents/clear_cache, /documents/upload|scan|file_batch|texts — which are rare, high-consequence operations. The DELETE-against-/documents shape is the corpus-wipe primitive the PoC demonstrated returning HTTP 200. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f4vv-55c2-5789 • https://cve.threatint.eu/CVE/CVE-2026-61740
ATT&CKT1485 T1496 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Administrator performing a legitimate corpus refresh (bulk /documents/upload or /documents/scan) during scheduled re-ingestion
  • Operational runbook clearing caches via /documents/clear_cache after a model/embedding change
  • A data pipeline that deletes and reloads the knowledge base on a schedule (DELETE /documents followed by re-upload)
  • CI / staging environments exercising the document API during automated tests
  • Backup/migration tooling snapshotting then clearing the document store
Suppression filter
| where RequestMethod =~ "DELETE"   // narrow to the pure corpus-destruction primitive, dropping benign upload/scan/cache-clear ingestion noise
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Identify the SourceIP and RequestMethod/RequestURL; confirm whether the call carried an X-API-Key (legitimate ops) or was preceded by a Bearer guest-JWT request (UC1) from the same IP — the latter confirms CVE-2026-61740 abuse. Check whether a change window/runbook explains it. 2) CONTAIN: Block the SourceIP, take the LightRAG instance off the public interface, and upgrade to lightrag-hku >=1.5.4; rotate TOKEN_SECRET and LIGHTRAG_API_KEY. 3) HUNT: Enumerate every document/graph/query call from that IP to quantify what was read, deleted, ingested (potential poisoning) or queried (LLM-credit exhaustion), and diff the current document store against the last backup to assess destruction.

| where (RequestMethod =~ "DELETE" and RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)/documents/?($|\?)")   // corpus wipe

| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction, DeviceProduct
